### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c1011b01bc071c545f72f2761647b8d9ab56375` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3a7f45112fb25ce1a9c60580e2a99c2da8d75d86` — the merge of head `2d75a59332ddea43798e08ebe82016359c972f52` into base `2c1011b01bc071c545f72f2761647b8d9ab56375`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3a7f45112fb25ce1a9c60580e2a99c2da8d75d86 && git checkout 3a7f45112fb25ce1a9c60580e2a99c2da8d75d86
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2c1011b01bc071c545f72f2761647b8d9ab56375 2d75a59332ddea43798e08ebe82016359c972f52 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2c1011b01bc071c545f72f2761647b8d9ab56375 && git merge --no-ff 2d75a59332ddea43798e08ebe82016359c972f52

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c1011b01bc071c545f72f2761647b8d9ab56375
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2d75a59332ddea43798e08ebe82016359c972f52`

### ① Derived judgments

1. `settleReadonlyWhenDrops` now settles the judged keys in strongly connected components (Tarjan) of "k's predicate reads j through `record`", in dependency order. `settleLockGroup` judges a one-key group once, against the final drops of the groups before it, and runs the fixpoint, release and fallback for a cycle only. RIGHT.
2. Single-row updates: a caller field whose lock is in no cycle is stored exactly when its lock is FALSE on the row the update stores, and ignored exactly when TRUE. The card's `x` now lands. Measured: the real engine at head stores `x: xv` where base stored `x: old`. The reviewer's own probe found 0 kept keys locked on the stored row and 0 dropped-while-unlocked keys outside a cycle, across 11,885 random lock systems. RIGHT.
3. Bulk updates: the same holds with "locked in at least one matched row", across 2,963 bulk systems and six bulk pins. RIGHT.
4. Master-detail: `engine.ts` is unchanged; `settleMasterDetailLanding` still judges the FK, now through the grouped settlement. The invoice example moves the line to `h_open`, stores `amt`, and ignores `c, y, a, b`. RIGHT.
5. `onFieldsDropped` / `strictReadonlyWrites` now name only the fields actually ignored. Whether a write is refused is unchanged: 0 of 11,885 differ. RIGHT.
6. No lock opens: 0 of 11,885, and no spelling in a 20-spelling battery let a locked field land. RIGHT.
7. The read-set extraction is conservative. A field is named only for a `.` / `.?` select on the bare `record` root; any other use of `record`, a non-CEL dialect or a parse failure counts as reading every field. Verified against the cel-js 8.0.0 AST for 37 sources, including `record['b']`, `size(record)`, macros, `dyn(record).a` and `'a' in record`. RIGHT.
8. Deterministic, and independent of declaration and payload order: 0 of 11,885 differ with both orders shuffled. RIGHT.
9. The per-cycle fallback is bounded; the loop bounds match the docblock. RIGHT.
10. Acyclic parity with base: 0 differences across 8,754 acyclic systems. All 13 moved answers are inside cycles, in the fail-safe direction. The dev's acceptance-note example reproduces. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` with `Clause-②: no` is consistent. No authorable key, export or error code moves: the new functions are module-private, and `engine.ts` and `packages/spec` are untouched. Every movement goes toward the cited `fields.mdx` text. Check-runs at head: 34 runs, 30 success, 3 skipped, 1 failure. The failure is `Check Changeset`, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class of `check-empty-changeset.mjs`, red by design pending written confirmation. All seven required contexts are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. `.changeset/19929-readonlywhen-cycle-isolation.md`: every factual sentence and worked example holds on measurement (c/x/y beside a/b; the two-agreeing-sets case; the invoice case; the `z` / `w` case; the `record['b']` / `size(record)` sentence; the `onFieldsDropped` sentences). No false or unmeasured sentence. One imprecision, not a FAIL: "counts as reading every field the update writes" is implemented as an edge to every other judged key, which has the same consumer-visible effect.
2. The corrected note, `.changeset/19911-readonlywhen-interdependent-locks.md` (pending; a DELIBERATE CORRECTION under `check-empty-changeset.mjs`). Each rewritten sentence is judged against the code at this head:
   - "A lock is judged after the locks whose fields it reads, with each value they drop put back to the row's stored one." TRUE: dependency order of the SCC groups, `withoutKeys(stored, dropped)`.
   - "Locks that read each other in a cycle are judged together, again with each dropped value put back, until no further field locks." TRUE: the cycle fixpoint in `settleLockGroup`.
   - "Then the fields held only by a value that was later put back are released, and every lock in the cycle is judged again against what that release stores, round after round, until the dropped fields are exactly the ones locked on the row the update stores." TRUE: the release rounds, scoped to the cycle.
   - "after one round more than the cycle has fields, the first, larger set of drops stands for the cycle's fields instead." TRUE: the first release set plus m sets, then the fixpoint set for that group's keys only.
   - "only when its lock is in a cycle of locks that read each other's fields (a `parent`-scoped lock counts as reading the master-detail field …, and a lock that reads `record` other than as `record.FIELD` counts as reading every field)." TRUE: `recordFieldsRead`; both conventions measured.
   - "A field whose lock is in no such cycle is dropped exactly when its lock is TRUE on the row the update stores (on a bulk update, on at least one matched row)." TRUE: 0 of 11,885 violations, single-row and bulk.
   - "Where a cycle's drops do not settle, the first, larger set stands for that cycle's fields: a lock the update cannot settle is not waived." TRUE.
   - The untouched paragraphs, including the `a`/`b` no-set and two-set examples: head drops both in each, and they stay pinned by the #19911 suite.
3. Dev open question (the 19911 correction): option A is right. Restoring the base text would republish a whole-update bound and fallback the shipped code no longer has.
4. Dev deviations are all real and sound:
   - SCC is better than connected components (the `out_of_cycle` pin shows the difference).
   - The H3 wording flag is honest; the invariant actually measured is the contract's.
   - The 4-in-16,500 delta is real, cycle keys only and fail-safe, and is stated in both changesets.
5. Dev out-of-scope observations: both are real and neither is a filing class. The `fields.mdx` silence on cycle over-locking is a docs gap. The payload-order `onFieldsDropped` listing is pre-existing and pinned.
6. The tests pin the fix and can fail: 18 of 18 red against the merge-base validator. The `every = true` to `every = false` ablation reddens exactly the two index-read pins.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19929-readonlywhen-per-component-fallback`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Isolated reviewer: a separate contract-review-tier subagent, fed the card, the parent card, the PR, `fields.mdx` and AGENTS.md only; adopted by the seat.

## Pending release-note correction on this PR: `Check Changeset` is red by design, awaiting written confirmation

`domain:engine#1`, `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`, written 2026-09-24T14:31Z.

Per `check-empty-changeset.mjs` (the foreign changeset rule, DELIBERATE CORRECTION class) and `pr-automation.yml` route 0, this PR names the note it corrects and what changed under it, here, and leaves `Check Changeset` red until that is confirmed in writing.

- **The note:** `.changeset/19911-readonlywhen-interdependent-locks.md`. It is PENDING: on `main`, not yet consumed by a release. It was added by PR #19923 (#19911).
- **What changed under it:** that note says drops that do not settle fall back to "the first, larger set of drops" for the WHOLE update, and that a field whose lock is FALSE can be dropped "only where locks read each other in a cycle". The second sentence holds per update, not per field. This PR settles locks cycle by cycle, so both sentences would be false for the shipped code. The PR rewrites exactly those two passages (+18 / −14) to describe the per-cycle settlement; nothing else in the note moves.
- **Why not restore it:** restoring the base text republishes, into `@objectstack/objectql`'s CHANGELOG, a whole-update bound and fallback that the code no longer has.
- **Verified:** the isolated contract review of record at this head (`2d75a593`) judged every rewritten sentence TRUE against the code and a fresh probe.
- **Not applied, per ruling D on #18375:** `skip-changeset`. This PR also releases its own change under `.changeset/19929-readonlywhen-cycle-isolation.md`.

**Confirmation, per ruling 1A** (#19940, record 5814546887, batch #220 item 3, maintainer 2026-09-24T12:56Z): 「an at-tier contract-review PASS record on the **same head** that names the corrected note and judges each rewritten sentence **is** the confirmation. The seat enqueues under the three-condition red-by-design path.」 That record is 5816146511 at `2d75a593`. The three conditions: ① the gate states it stays red by design (`check-empty-changeset.mjs`, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class); ② `Check Changeset` runs in `pr-automation.yml`, which triggers on `pull_request` only, never `merge_group`; ③ this comment records the gate and the reason. (Superseded wording: an earlier revision of this comment routed the confirmation to the decision box. It was written before the seat read ruling 1A.)
